info.title: Screeps community server socket API
info.description: Socket protocol of the stock Screeps private server (screeps/backend-local without mods) as the official web client uses it when `options.official` is false. Composed from the official Screeps World socket contract and the community compatibility profile; each message's `x-profile` states whether it is unchanged (`required`) or has documented differences (`adapted`). Channel names carry no shard. The socket does not check the server password. Session tokens are short-lived: every `auth ok` and every authenticated HTTP response issues a replacement that must be stored.

externalDocs.description: Pinned source provenance, coverage and the standalone compatibility profile

community.description: SockJS endpoint `/socket` of the private server; the raw WebSocket transport is `/socket/websocket`. Use `wss` when a proxy terminates TLS.

host.description: Private server hostname or IP address.

port.description: Private server HTTP port (`GAME_PORT`, 21025 by default).

socket.title: Socket connection
socket.description: The raw WebSocket transport of the SockJS endpoint; one connection multiplexes every message below. Channel events are JSON text `[channel, data]`; `err@<channel>` instead of `<channel>` marks an error event of that channel. Any channel event may arrive as a `gz:` compressed frame after `gzip on`. Text that starts with `[` is a channel event; everything else is a protocol line. Subscription channel names are case-sensitive and must be sent exactly as described by each event message.

receiveAuth.title: Authenticate a connection
receiveAuth.description: The server checks the token and replies on the same connection. A failed attempt is answered with `auth failed`; whether an earlier successful authentication of the same connection stays in effect afterwards is not evidenced, so clients authenticate once per connection.

receiveGzip.title: Toggle compression
receiveGzip.summary: Clients opt in to compressed channel events.
receiveGzip.description: There is no acknowledgement; later channel events may arrive as `gz:` frames.

receiveSubscribe.title: Subscribe to a channel
receiveSubscribe.summary: Clients subscribe to one channel per command.
receiveSubscribe.description: Events of the channel follow as channel event messages. There is no acknowledgement.

receiveUnsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe from a channel
receiveUnsubscribe.summary: Clients unsubscribe from one channel per command.

sendCompressedEvents.title: Send compressed channel events
sendCompressedEvents.summary: Any channel event can arrive compressed after `gzip on`.
sendCompressedEvents.description: Inflate, then handle the result like an uncompressed channel event.

sendGreeting.title: Greet a new connection
sendGreeting.summary: The server announces its clock and versions as soon as a connection opens.
sendGreeting.description: Sent in this order, uncompressed, before any reply to client commands.

sendRoomEvents.title: Publish room and map updates
sendRoomEvents.summary: Room diffs, room map views and map visuals after each tick.
sendRoomEvents.description: Updates are throttled and follow game ticks; a connection that falls behind receives a later diff covering skipped ticks.

sendUserEvents.title: Publish account events
sendUserEvents.description: Only the authenticated user's own `user:<id>/...` channels are served.

auth.name: auth
auth.title: Authenticate
auth.summary: Sign the connection in with an API or session token.
auth.description: Client command `auth <token>`, using the same token as the HTTP `X-Token` header. The official client sends it as soon as the connection opens when signed in (anonymous clients skip it). The server answers with `auth ok <token>` or `auth failed`.

authFailed.name: authFailed
authFailed.title: Authentication failed
authFailed.summary: Reply to `auth` when the token is not accepted.
authFailed.description: Unframed protocol line `auth failed`, sent uncompressed. The connection stays open and anonymous: the official client still sends its queued subscriptions, of which only public ones (`server-message`) are served.

authOk.name: authOk
authOk.title: Authentication succeeded
authOk.summary: Reply to `auth`: the connection is signed in; carries the token to keep using.
authOk.description: Unframed protocol line `auth ok <token>`, sent uncompressed. The token is a newly issued session token (40 hex characters) that expires after 60 seconds unless an authenticated HTTP request rotates it again; store it in place of the sent token for later `auth` commands and HTTP requests. The official client replaces its stored token with it, then sends the subscriptions it queued.

x-profile.reason: backend-local tokens are session tokens: `auth ok` issues a new one, stored for 60 seconds, that replaces the stored token.

compressedFrame.name: compressedFrame
compressedFrame.title: Compressed event
compressedFrame.summary: A channel event compressed after `gzip on`.
compressedFrame.description: `gz:` followed by the base64 encoding of a zlib (RFC 1950) deflate stream. Inflating it yields the UTF-8 text of exactly one channel event (`[channel, data]`). The server compresses channel events only while the client has `gzip on` and only when the encoded form is shorter; protocol lines (`time`, `protocol`, `package`, `auth ...`) are never compressed. The official client inflates with `pako.ungzip`, which also accepts gzip (RFC 1952) streams.

gzip.name: gzip
gzip.title: Toggle compression
gzip.summary: Enable or disable compressed channel events for this connection.
gzip.description: Client command `gzip on` or `gzip off` (default off). While on, the server may send channel events as `gz:` frames; clients must accept both forms either way. The official client sends `gzip on` right after opening when configured to.

mapVisualEvent.name: mapVisualEvent
mapVisualEvent.title: Map visuals
mapVisualEvent.summary: The subscribing user's map visuals of the previous tick (`mapVisual:<user>`).
mapVisualEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. Data is the map visual string of the previous tick: newline-terminated JSON lines, each a `MapVisualItem`, or `null` when there are none.

x-profile.reason: One world: the map visual channel is `mapVisual:<user>` without a shard.

protocol.name: protocol
protocol.title: Protocol version
protocol.description: Unframed protocol line `protocol <integer>`, sent uncompressed after `time`. The value matches `protocol` of `GET /api/version`; screeps.com reported 14.

roomErrorEvent.name: roomErrorEvent
roomErrorEvent.title: Room subscription skipped
roomErrorEvent.description: Sent instead of a room update when the user exceeds the room subscription limit for that update (data `subscribe limit reached`). The subscription stays registered. The official client routes `err@<channel>` to the error handler of `<channel>`.

x-profile.reason: One world: the room error channel is `err@room:<room>` without a shard.

roomEvent.name: roomEvent
roomEvent.title: Room update
roomEvent.summary: Detailed, incremental updates of one room (`room:<room>`).
roomEvent.description: Requires authentication. The first event after subscribing is the full room; later events are diffs against what this connection already received (see `RoomObjectsDiff`), sent at most once per tick. Each user receives at most two room subscriptions per update across all connections; subscriptions beyond that receive `err@room:` events instead and resume when selected again. Rooms that do not exist are ignored silently.

x-profile.reason: One world: the room channel is `room:<room>` without a shard; room events carry no `decorations`, and their `users` entries are the users' complete stored documents.

roomMapEvent.name: roomMapEvent
roomMapEvent.title: Room map view
roomMapEvent.summary: Low-detail positions of one room for the world map (`roomMap2:<room>`).
roomMapEvent.description: Requires authentication. Sent right after subscribing and then with every update; each event is complete (not a diff).

x-profile.reason: One world: the map channel is `roomMap2:<room>` without a shard.

serverMessageEvent.name: serverMessageEvent
serverMessageEvent.title: Server announcement
serverMessageEvent.description: Event of the public `server-message` channel, which accepts anonymous subscriptions. The official client shows the data in a dialog.
serverMessageEvent.x-unverified: Not observed live; the data type is evidenced by the private-server announcement command (a text string) only.

subscribe.name: subscribe
subscribe.title: Subscribe
subscribe.summary: Start receiving events of one channel.
subscribe.description: Client command `subscribe <channel>`. Send after `auth ok`: user and room channels sent before authentication are rejected, and rejections are silent (no event ever arrives). A channel of another user is rejected. Subscribing again to a channel already subscribed on the same connection is not idempotent on every server implementation (room channels can be delivered twice); clients keep one subscription per channel and connection. Several channels publish an initial event right after subscribing (`room:`, `roomMap2:`, `mapVisual:`, `user:<id>/cpu`, `user:<id>/memory/...`).

time.name: time
time.title: Server time
time.summary: Server clock in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, sent first on every connection.
time.description: Unframed protocol line `time <milliseconds>`. Sent uncompressed immediately after the connection opens, before any client command. The official client stores the difference to its own clock as a time correction.

unsubscribe.name: unsubscribe
unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe
unsubscribe.summary: Stop receiving events of one channel.
unsubscribe.description: Client command `unsubscribe <channel>`. The official client only unsubscribes channels it actually subscribed on the current connection. Events already in flight may still arrive.

userCodeEvent.name: userCodeEvent
userCodeEvent.title: Code saved
userCodeEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. Sent when a branch of the account is saved.
userCodeEvent.x-unverified: Not observed live (no code was saved during observation). The event re-reads the stored branch, whose save times were observed through `GET /api/user/branches?withCode=true` (2026-10-17): milliseconds, and an ISO 8601 string for a branch created by `POST /api/user/clone-branch`.

userConsoleEvent.name: userConsoleEvent
userConsoleEvent.title: Console output
userConsoleEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. One output event per run of each shard (empty lists included); a run error is an additional, separate event.
userConsoleEvent.x-unverified: Whether run error events always carry `shard` on screeps.com is not observed.

x-profile.reason: One world: console events carry no `shard`.

userCpuEvent.name: userCpuEvent
userCpuEvent.title: CPU usage
userCpuEvent.summary: CPU and Memory usage of each run (`user:<user>/cpu`).
userCpuEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. Sent right after subscribing (with `cpu` 0) and then for runs, throttled.
userCpuEvent.x-unverified: `cpu` as the string `error` (CPU limit reached) comes from the private-server runtime and was not observed on screeps.com; `memory` was present in every observed event.

userMemoryEvent.name: userMemoryEvent
userMemoryEvent.title: Memory watch
userMemoryEvent.summary: The value at one Memory path (`user:<user>/memory/<path>`).
userMemoryEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. `<path>` is dot-separated. Sent with every update for the first fifty paths of a user. Data is the JavaScript string conversion of the value: `undefined` when absent, `[object Object]` for objects, and `Incorrect memory path` when the path cannot be traversed. Read whole values over HTTP (`GET /api/user/memory`) instead.

x-profile.reason: One world: Memory watch channels are `user:<user>/memory/<path>` without a shard.

userMessageEvent.name: userMessageEvent
userMessageEvent.title: Conversation update
userMessageEvent.summary: A message of one conversation was sent or marked read (`user:<user>/message:<respondent>`).
userMessageEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. `<respondent>` is the other participant's user id. A sent message carries the complete copy of `<user>`; marking read carries only `_id` and `unread`.
userMessageEvent.x-unverified: Not observed live (no conversation changed during observation).

userNewMessageEvent.name: userNewMessageEvent
userNewMessageEvent.title: New private message
userNewMessageEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. Data holds the recipient's copy of the message.
userNewMessageEvent.x-unverified: Not observed live (no message was received during observation).

userResourcesEvent.name: userResourcesEvent
userResourcesEvent.title: Account resources
userResourcesEvent.description: Requires authentication as `<user>`. Sent with every update; each event is complete.

userSetActiveBranchEvent.name: userSetActiveBranchEvent
userSetActiveBranchEvent.title: Active branch changed
userSetActiveBranchEvent.summary: The world or simulation branch changed (`user:<user>/set-active-branch`).
userSetActiveBranchEvent.x-unverified: Not observed live (no branch was activated during observation).

RoomEvent.description: One room update. The first event after subscribing carries `users` (including the built-in users) and `info`, plus `flags` when the subscribing user has flags in the room; later events carry `objects`, `gameTime` and `visual`, `info` for world rooms (`W1N1`-style names), `flags` when the subscribing user has flags, and `users` when objects reference users not sent before. `users` entries are the referenced users' complete stored documents (the default storage ignores the requested `username`/`badge` projection), including private fields such as `email`. The official client shallow-merges `users` into the users it holds.

users.description: Users not yet sent on this subscription, keyed by user id.

flags.description: The subscribing user's flags in this room: entries joined by `|`, each `name~color~secondaryColor~x~y`, where `|` and `~` inside a name are written as `$VLINE$` and `$TILDE$`. `null` when the user has no flags; absent from events that do not change them.

visual.description: The subscribing user's room visuals of the previous tick, global visuals first: newline-terminated JSON lines, each a `RoomVisualItem`; empty when none.

RoomEvent.x-profile-reason: Room events of backend-local carry no `decorations`, and `users` holds complete stored user documents.

RoomMap.description: Low-detail room view for map rendering: each key lists the positions of one kind of object. Every key that is not one of the documented kinds is a user id listing that user's creeps and structures (the official client colours each such key separately). An empty object means no view is stored for the room. Kinds: `w` constructed walls, `r` roads, `pb` power banks, `p` portals, `s` sources, `c` controllers, `m` minerals, `k` keeper lairs.

RoomObject.description: A complete room object, as sent for an id the client does not hold yet; the same document `GET /api/game/room-objects` returns (`GameRoomObject`), discriminated by `type`. Each described type has its own schema; dropped resources use `RoomObjectResource` and any other `type` validates as `RoomObjectOther`.

RoomObjectActionLog.description: Actions of the last tick keyed by action (`attack`, `attacked`, `attackController`, `build`, `harvest`, `heal`, `healed`, `power`, `produce`, `rangedAttack`, `rangedHeal`, `rangedMassAttack`, `repair`, `reserveController`, `reverseReaction`, `runReaction`, `say`, `spawned`, `transferEnergy`, `upgradeController`, …). An entry is `null` when the action did not happen; `spawned: true` marks a power creep spawned in the last tick.

RoomObjectPatch.description: Changes to a room object the client holds, merged into it (see `RoomObjectsDiff`). Only changed properties are present and `null` marks a removed or cleared property. Top-level arrays (`body`, `creepBody`, `depositTypes`, and `effects` or `population` in array form) arrive either whole or as an object of the changed elements keyed by array index, because the client merges them index-wise; nested objects hold only their changed properties. A complete `RoomObject` is also a valid patch.

RoomObjectsDiff.description: Room object changes keyed by object id. Apply each entry in order (official client `U`/`N`): `null` removes the held object; an id the client does not hold carries a complete `RoomObject`, which the client adds; for a held object the value is a `RoomObjectPatch`: first convert every top-level array property of both the held object and the patch into an object keyed by array index, then deep-merge the patch into the held object with lodash 3 `_.merge` semantics, except that an array merged into an array replaces it. A property set to `null` means the property was removed or cleared. The first event after subscribing holds every object of the room; later events hold only changes since the previous event delivered to this connection.

RoomVisualItem.description: One item of a room visual string (one JSON line), as written by `RoomVisual` (`t`: `l` line, `c` circle, `r` rect, `p` poly, `t` text). Coordinates are room tiles and may be fractional. The game does not validate drawing arguments, and `RoomVisual.import` appends arbitrary text, so lines of other shapes are possible.
